Arba
AR-bah
n. (proper, the greatest of the Anakims; Hebrew, four)
Hebrew Arba, four. He gave his name to Kirjath-arba, the city of Arba, which Israel afterwards called Hebron — the place of Abraham's grave and of David's first throne.

Biblical Definition

Joshua tells us who he was in an aside: “And the name of Hebron before was Kirjatharba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war” (Joshua 14:15). The verse before it records Caleb receiving Hebron for an inheritance at eighty-five, because he wholly followed the LORD God of Israel. Twice more the city is described by the man: Caleb was given “the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron” (Joshua 15:13), and the priests received “the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with the suburbs thereof” (Joshua 21:11). The ten spies had come back from this very place saying they were as grasshoppers in the sight of the Anakims. Forty-five years later the old man who had said we are well able to overcome it asked for that mountain and took it, and a city named after a giant became a city of refuge and of priests.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a great man among the Anakims, the father of Anak, whose city Kirjath-arba became Hebron.

expand to see more

ANAKIM, n. In Scripture, a race of giants who dwelt in the hill country of Canaan, especially about Hebron.

GIANT, n. A man of extraordinary bulk and stature; in Scripture, one of a race of unusual size and strength.

HEBRON, n. An ancient city of Judah in the hill country, the burial place of the patriarchs and David's first capital.

REFUGE, n. Shelter or protection from danger or distress; in Israel, a city appointed for the manslayer to flee to.

INHERITANCE, n. An estate derived from an ancestor to an heir; in Scripture, the portion of a tribe or family in the land.

Key Scripture

Joshua 14:15 — "And the name of Hebron before was Kirjatharba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war."

Joshua 15:13 — "And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the LORD to Joshua, even the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. the"

Joshua 21:11 — "And they gave them the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with the suburbs thereof round about it. the"

Joshua 14:12 — "Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the LORD will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the LORD said."

Modern Corruption

Obstacles are sized up by the resources of the one facing them, which is exactly the arithmetic of the ten spies; Caleb measured the same giants against the promise of God and asked for their mountain at eighty-five.

expand to see more

Numbers 13 and Joshua 14 describe the same city and reach opposite conclusions. The ten spies reported walled cities, great and tall men, the children of Anak, and said we be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we. Caleb saw the identical giants and said the identical facts and added one more: the LORD is with us. The difference was not optimism against pessimism but arithmetic with God left out against arithmetic with God in. Forty-five years later he was still asking for that hill: Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spake in that day.

The result is worth sitting with. A city named for the greatest of the Anakims became Hebron, the burial place of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, a city of refuge for the manslayer, a priests' city, and the place where David reigned seven years before Jerusalem. The stronghold of a giant was turned into a sanctuary for the weak. That reversal is the pattern of redemption in miniature, and it began with one old man who wholly followed the LORD when everyone else did the sums without him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Arba (H704), four; Qiryath Arba (H7153), city of Arba; Anaq (H6061), Anak, long-necked; Chebrown (H2275), Hebron, fellowship.

expand to see more

Hebrew Arba (H704) — Arba, four; a great man among the Anakims.

Hebrew Qiryath Arba (H7153) — Kirjath-arba, the city of Arba; Hebron's older name.

Hebrew Anaq (H6061) — Anak, long-necked; the giant stock that terrified the ten spies.

Hebrew Chebrown (H2275) — Hebron, from chabar, to join; association or fellowship.

Hebrew male achar — to fill up after, to wholly follow; said of Caleb five times.

Usage

"“Which Arba was a great man among the Anakims” — the city's namesake."

"“The city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron”."

"“Now therefore give me this mountain” — Caleb at eighty-five."
